title: SLO-driven disaster recovery drill orchestration and snapshot-restore validation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible, SLO-aware active->passive failover drill runbook and automated snapshot-restore validation suite. This ticket covers: runbook authoring, orchestration tooling for scheduled drills, scripted backup verification, traffic cutover and rollback steps, circuit breaker and load-shedding validation, observable success/failure criteria tied to SLOs, and post-drill postmortem templates. Goal: prove that critical inference paths can be restored and failover completed within RTO=5m and RPO<=15m in the majority (>95%) of scheduled drills, and produce a remediation plan for recurrent failures.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook versioned and committed in Confluence + repo (runbook v1.0)
Automated drill orchestration that can be scheduled and run from CI with a single command
Snapshot restore verification scripts that validate data integrity and KV-cache warmup within defined thresholds
Circuit breaker and load-shedding policies exercised and proven to keep tail latency under SLO during simulated overload
Successful end-to-end dry run with RTO <= 5 minutes observed and documented; issues logged if not met
Post-drill postmortem template filled and follow-ups scheduled for any failure modes
steps: Pre-drill: validate latest backups exist and pass checksum; ensure snapshots are >3 copies in different AZs/regions
Pre-drill: confirm canary traffic routing plan and health-check endpoints; create a temporary canary token with limited scope
Pre-drill: freeze non-essential deployments and schedule maintenance windows with stakeholders
Kick-off: trigger orchestration job that creates a fresh passive recovery cluster (in secondary region) from latest snapshots
Data-restore: run automated restore scripts, validate table counts, kv-store keys, and model artifact checksums
KV cache warmup: replay a curated prefix set to pre-warm caches; measure cold-to-warm latency profile
Traffic cutover: shift 1% canary traffic using traffic-router, validate traces and latency, then step to 10%, 50%, 100% following SLO gates
Circuit breakers: induce controlled backend overload (throttled) and verify CBs open and shed load according to policy; confirm graceful degradation responses
Load shedding: apply priority-based load-shedding rules and observe failure rates for low-priority requests remain within tolerance
Rollback: on SLO gate failure, execute scripted rollback to primary with clear rollback checklist
Post-drill: capture metrics, traces, and synthetic prompt evaluation scripts for quality regression checks
Postmortem: fill template, assign action items, and schedule remediation sprints for systemic issues
observability_checks: SLO dashboard: 99th/95th/50th latency, error rate, availability for inference endpoints
Traffic-router health and per-region capacity metrics
Restore validation dashboard: snapshot size, restore time, checksum pass/fail
KV cache hit-rate and warmup latency curves
Circuit breaker metrics: open/close counts, fallback counts
Load-shedding counters: requests dropped by policy and per-priority QoS metrics
Synthetic evals: prompt suites with golden responses and quality score deltas
test_results_summary: Dry run 2025-11-13: automated restore completed in 4m12s (within RTO), KV cache warmup reached 85% hit-rate after 6 minutes (slower than target), canary traffic cutover succeeded to 10% but failed SLO at 50% due to backend queuing under heavy burst. Root cause: kernel scheduling on dedicated GPUs delayed small-batch requests under cold start. Action items created to tune batcher thresholds and add pre-warm hooks.
